[[Ngendan languages|Ngendan]]? |iso3=boy |glotto=bodo1272 |glottorefname=Bodo (Central African Republic) |guthrie=D.308 }} '''Bodo''' is a possibly extinct [[Bantu language]] of the [[Central African Republic]]. It may be part of a group of languages called "[[Lebonya languages|Lebonya]]".{{citation needed|date=February 2025}} [[UNESCO]] lists Bodo as "severely endangered".{{cite web |author= |date=2021 |title= Bodo (Central African Republic) |url=https://en.wal.unesco.org/languages/bodo-central-african-republic |website=[[Atlas of the World's Languages in Danger|World Atlas of Languages]] |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=19 February 2025}} It reportedly has or had 15 speakers, who lived scattered throughout the country.{{cite book |last=Connell |first=Bruce |date=2007 |editor-last=Brenzinger |editor-first=Matthias |title=Language Diversity Endangered |publisher=[[De Gruyter|De Gruyter Mouton]] |pages=175 |chapter=Chapter 8: Endangered Languages in Central Africa |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9783110197129.163/html |isbn=9783110170498 |doi=10.1515/9783110197129.163 |access-date=19 February 2025}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Narrow Bantu languages (Zones C–D)}} {{authority control}} [[Category:Lebonya languages]] [[Category:Languages of the Central African Republic]] [[Category:Endangered Niger–Congo languages]] {{Bantu-lang-stub}}
